facts.text: Extending a validated model to another machine model or sensor position means identifying changes, assessing whether they affect validated phenomena, and closing gaps with targeted bridging tests; validation is never inherited automatically.
facts.quote: A model validated on one machine is extended to another by showing what changed, whether the change can affect a validated phenomenon, and what targeted bridging tests close the gap; it is never inherited automatically.

facts.text: Rail, aviation, nuclear and medical practice formalize model transfer as validation-domain extension through similarity and bridging evidence, rather than automatically transferring validation from Model A to Model B.
facts.quote: validation-domain extension by similarity plus bridging evidence, not "Model A was validated, therefore Model B is validated". Rail, aviation, nuclear and medical practice all formalize this

facts.text: No published off-road example of variant transfer was found.
facts.quote: no published off-road example of variant transfer was found [Chapter 10]

facts.text: The booklet recommends a parameterized family model rather than 20 unrelated models, with parameters including geometry and articulation, mass and payload, brake dynamics, sensor type, mounting height and angle, vibration and latency.
facts.quote: a parameterized family model rather than 20 unrelated models, with parameters such as geometry and articulation, mass and payload, brake dynamics, sensor type, mounting height and angle, vibration and latency

facts.text: The booklet recommends validating a parameterized machine-family model at envelope corners: the smallest and largest machine, lowest and highest sensor mount, and lowest and highest mass.
facts.quote: validated at the corners of the envelope (smallest and largest machine, lowest and highest mount, lowest and highest mass)

facts.text: For each new machine variant, the recommended safety case identifies what changed using a configuration-controlled delta.
facts.quote: For each new variant the safety case answers three questions: what changed (a configuration-controlled delta)

facts.text: For each new machine variant, the recommended safety case uses sensitivity analysis and uncertainty propagation to assess whether changes can affect a validated phenomenon or safety output.
facts.quote: can that change affect a validated phenomenon or safety output (sensitivity analysis and uncertainty propagation)

facts.text: For each new machine variant, the recommended bridging evidence is none for irrelevant differences, targeted component tests for influential differences, and new full-system anchors where new physics appear.
facts.quote: what bridging evidence closes the gap (none for irrelevant differences, targeted component tests for influential ones, new full-system anchors where new physics appear)

facts.text: A machine variant inside the validated hull receives a reduced delta test set consisting of brake calibration plus a sensor field-of-view and detection check at the new mount.
facts.quote: A variant inside the validated hull gets a reduced delta set: brake calibration plus a sensor field-of-view and detection check at the new mount.

facts.text: A machine variant outside the validated hull, or introducing a new phenomenon such as articulated steering, is re-validated.
facts.quote: A variant outside the hull, or one introducing a new phenomenon such as articulated steering, is re-validated [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Sensor relocation requires special caution because moving unchanged sensor hardware changes occlusion, angle of incidence, ground returns, vibration and contamination patterns; sensor pose is therefore a model input with its own validated range.
facts.quote: even with unchanged hardware, moving a sensor changes occlusion, angle of incidence, ground returns, vibration and contamination patterns, so sensor pose is a model input with its own validated range [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Machine-model portability is an experiment rather than an established fact: the machine-variant portability test checks whether a second, substantially different model requires parameterization or redevelopment.
facts.quote: Portability is a key experiment, not a fact: the "machine-variant portability test" checks whether a second, substantially different model is parameterization or redevelopment.

facts.text: The claim that chosen machine extremes bound all intermediate machines must be demonstrated because geometry and occlusion can create non-monotonic effects.
facts.quote: The claim that chosen extremes bound all intermediate machines must itself be demonstrated, because geometry and occlusion can create non-monotonic effects [Chapters 10, 13].
